channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio treina respostas a jornalistas e se justifica para base partidária
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign has entered 'damage control' mode following recent controversies, with the presidential pre-candidate training responses to journalists and justifying himself to the party base. The goal is to mitigate negative impacts and strengthen internal support amid media and opposition pressure.

item.title: Caso Banco Master: PF faz operação contra perito que teria vazado dados à imprensa
item.description: The Federal Police conducted an operation in Rondônia to investigate a leak of confidential information by a federal forensic expert linked to Operation Compliance Zero, which probes alleged billion-dollar frauds at Banco Master. The expert allegedly passed secret data to a journalist in December 2024 and January 2025, unrelated to the Intercept audio leaks involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro. The STF issued precautionary measures, including suspension of the officer’s duties, emphasizing the probe targets public officials, not journalists or press freedom.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Flávio derrete; Neymar convocado
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discusses the impact of leaked audio involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) on the 2026 electoral race, suggesting his image is deteriorating. It also covers a new Federal Police operation targeting leaks in the Compliance Zero investigation and Neymar's call-up to the Brazilian national football team.

item.title: 51,7% ligam Flávio ao caso Master após mensagens, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll shows 51.7% of Brazilian voters believe messages between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Master, constitute direct evidence of his involvement in the financial fraud case at the institution. Conducted May 13–18, 2026 among 5,032 respondents, the survey found 95.6% were aware of the leak and 93.9% had listened to the audio. Another 33.3% viewed the conversation as a legitimate effort to secure funding for the film “Dark Horse,” about Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: O dia mais difícil para Flávio: queda em pesquisa, reunião com a bancada e transferência de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces his most challenging day since announcing his presidential pre-candidacy, trailing Lula by 13 points in the AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll, convening an urgent meeting with the PL caucus to explain an audio in which he asked banker Daniel Vorcaro for funds for his father's biopic, and Vorcaro's transfer to a common cell, which restricts lawyer access and may pressure him into a plea deal.

item.title: José Guimarães diz que “taxa das blusinhas” foi erro do governo Lula
item.description: Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães (PT) stated that the so-called 'tax on little blouses' was an error of the Lula government, harming low-income families and the lower middle class, and that he worked internally to have it repealed. He also said the PT will use the scandal involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former banker Daniel Vorcaro as a central theme in the 2026 presidential campaign, asserting that the country needs to be 'cleaned up' and that Flávio Bolsonaro's image has 'collapsed' following the Intercept Brazil revelations.

item.title: CPI do Master: fala sério, Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro claims to support a congressional inquiry (CPI) into alleged irregularities in the Master case, but his statement is met with skepticism due to the Bolsonaro family’s history of using investigations for political purposes. The article suggests his position may be an attempt to deflect criticism or frame himself as a victim, without guaranteeing a genuine or impartial investigation. The context reflects internal political struggles and tensions within the Bolsonaro-aligned political faction.

item.title: Quaest: 32% dizem que reeleição de Lula é melhor resultado da eleição para o Brasil; 24% apontam retorno da família Bolsonaro; e 22%, vitória de outsider
item.description: Quaest poll shows 32% of voters view Lula’s re-election as the best outcome for Brazil in 2026, followed by 24% favoring the Bolsonaro family’s return and 22% supporting an outsider candidate. By asking about the 'best result' rather than voting intention, the poll minimizes the influence of strategic voting and reveals deeper ideological preferences. Among women, 33% prefer Lula; among men, he also leads, though with a narrower margin over Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Percepção sobre grupo político mais envolvido com o Master mudou
item.description: The leak of conversations between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Daniel Vorcaro shifted Brazilian voters' perception of which political group is most involved in the Master scandal, according to an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg survey. 'Bolsonaro's allies' are now seen as the most involved group by 43.3% of respondents, indicating a notable shift in public opinion.

item.title: Comissão debate impacto de resoluções do TSE nas eleições de 2026 para o setor de comunicações
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Communication Committee holds a public hearing to discuss the impact of new TSE resolutions on the 2026 elections for the communications sector, covering electoral propaganda, content boosting, and disinformation combat. Requested by Deputy Maria Rosas (Republicanos-SP), the debate takes place this Wednesday at 2 PM in Plenary 11 and includes broadcasters, press, news portals, and digital platforms.

item.title: O desconhecimento do eleitorado sobre a rejeição de Messias, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha survey released on May 19, 2026 shows that 59% of Brazilian voters were unaware that the Senate rejected Jorge Messias’ nomination to the Supreme Federal Court. Among the 41% who were aware, only 19% considered themselves well-informed, while 53% of those informed believe the rejection weakened Lula’s government. The poll surveyed 2,004 voters between May 12 and 13, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Deputado pede instauração de CPMI para investigar filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Federal Deputy Rogério Correia (PT-MG) has requested the establishment of a CPMI to investigate alleged irregularities in the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', a biopic of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The request cites potential financial contributions from businessman Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the Master scandal, and suspicions of money laundering, misuse of public funds, and irregular political financing through parliamentary amendments and São Paulo city contracts. The producer denies receiving the funds, while actor Jim Caviezel, known for far-right positions, portrays Bolsonaro in the film set for release in August 2026.

item.title: Federação PP e União Brasil discute liberar coligações nos estados ou optar por neutralidade na eleição presidencial
item.description: The PP and União Brasil federation is discussing national support for Flávio Bolsonaro but may allow state-level coalitions with other parties or opt for neutrality due to the ongoing controversy involving the senator and film producers over financing. Leaders acknowledge that backing Flávio came late and is contingent on no new scandals emerging, while the PL remains firmly aligned with him despite internal concerns about electoral risks. A final decision will be delayed until the case’s impact clarifies, with expectations of negative polling fluctuations in the next 10 to 15 days.

item.title: 45,1% dizem que conversas com Vorcaro enfraquecem muito Flávio
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows 45.1% of respondents believe the disclosure of conversations between Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro greatly weakened his presidential candidacy, rising to 64.1% when including those who saw a slight weakening. Meanwhile, 47.1% say they would no longer vote for him under any circumstances, while 84.2% of Jair Bolsonaro voters believe he should remain in the race.

item.title: Gonet, o minúsculo
item.description: Paulo Gonet, Brazil's Attorney General, denounced presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) for aggravated slander after Zema released a satirical video featuring puppets of Gilmar Mendes and Dias Toffoli, accusing them of passive corruption. The denunciation is seen as an authoritarian attempt to punish legitimate criticism, particularly given the PGR's pattern of archiving investigations against Supreme Court allies while acting selectively. The case highlights perceptions of PGR subservience to a judiciary faction in 2026.

item.title: Mesmo de férias, Jorge Messias acompanha Lula em agendas após presidente sinalizar reenvio de seu nome ao STF
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias accompanied President Lula in two agendas in São Paulo, despite being on vacation, after Lula signaled the possibility of resubmitting Messias' name to the STF. Lula is considering pushing for the nomination again despite the risk of another defeat, hoping for a rapprochement with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to overcome the current rule blocking reappraisal of rejected nominees in the same legislative year. So far, Lula has not made a final decision, and if the Senate norm is not overturned, the appointment would only be considered in 2025, after the presidential election.

item.title: O nível de contaminação de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll revealed that the messages exchanged between Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro negatively impacted public perception, benefiting Lula in voting intentions. After months of rising in the polls, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro saw his image tarnished by the scandal, which could harm his future candidacies.

item.title: AtlasIntel aponta queda na desaprovação a Lula; veja os resultados
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll released on May 19, 2026 shows a slight decline in disapproval of President Lula (PT), from 53% to 51.3%, while approval rose from 47% to 47.4%. Government evaluation improved, with 42.9% rating it as good or excellent (up from 42%) and 48.4% as poor or terrible (down from 51%). Among Catholics, Lula has 52.7% approval; among evangelicals, only 25.1%.

item.title: Lula está 7 pontos à frente de Flávio em eventual 2º turno, aponta pesquisa AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro by 7 points in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, according to an AtlasIntel poll released on May 19. The president reached 48.9% voting intention, while the senator dropped to 41.8% after audio leaks linking him to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. The survey shows rising rejection and fear of a Flávio victory, along with a shift in public perception regarding involvement in the Master scandal.

item.title: Datafolha: Maioria diz ser 'muito importante' indicar mulher ao STF; 46%, religioso, e 46%, pessoa negra
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows 51% of Brazilians consider it 'very important' to appoint a woman to the Supreme Court, with 46% saying the same for Black individuals and religious figures. Despite the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias, Lula plans to renominate him, drawing criticism for maintaining an 'exclusionary pattern' in a court that currently has only one female justice, Cármen Lúcia.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de evento da indústria da construção
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the opening of Enic 2026, the construction industry’s international meeting, in São Paulo, including a visit to stands of the ‘Se Essa Rua Fosse Minha’ program, a meeting with sector leaders, and the opening ceremony at 11h. BNDES President Aloizio Mercadante is also present. The event focuses on strengthening and expanding the construction sector in Brazil.

item.title: Aumento da rejeição e outras más notícias: o impacto dos áudios a Vorcaro para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The AtlasIntel poll revealed increased rejection of Flávio Bolsonaro following the leak of audios linking him to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of the Master bank. 52% of voters now say they would never vote for him, surpassing Lula’s rejection rate of 50.6%. Over 64% believe the scandal weakens his candidacy, and public perception has shifted, with more voters associating Bolsonarismo with the Master scheme.

item.title: 52% rejeitam votar em Flávio Bolsonaro e 50,6% em Lula
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll reveals 52% of voters would never vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 50.6% for Lula. Jair Bolsonaro is rejected by 49.1% and Michelle Bolsonaro by 45.6%. The survey, conducted May 13–18 with 5,032 respondents, has a 1-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Quem é Joaquim Barbosa, ministro aposentado do STF que será candidato a presidente
item.description: Joaquim Barbosa, former Supreme Court Justice and the first Black person to preside over the Court, has been announced as a pre-candidate for president by the Christian Democracy party (DC), replacing Aldo Rebelo after poor polling performance. His candidacy, revealed by Folha de S.Paulo and confirmed by JOTA, sparked internal party conflict but is backed by qualitative surveys in 15 states showing strong performance. Barbosa, 71, emphasizes his life journey — from humble origins in Paracatu (MG) to the STF — as qualification to foster harmony among Brazil’s powers and national stability.

item.title: 51,3% desaprovam e 47,4% aprovam o governo Lula, diz Atlas/Bloomberg
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll released on May 19, 2026 shows 51.3% of respondents disapprove of President Lula’s government, while 47.4% approve. Government evaluation is negative for 48.4% (bad/terrible), with only 42.9% rating it as excellent/good. The survey interviewed 5,032 Brazilian voters from May 13–18, with a 1 percentage point margin of error and TSE registration BR-06939/2026.

item.title: Lula tem 48,9% contra 41,8% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula leads the runoff with 48.9% of voting intentions against 41.8% for Flávio Bolsonaro, according to an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll conducted between May 13 and 18, 2026. The leak of messages in which the senator asked Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, for money negatively impacted Flávio's perception, with 65.2% of respondents saying they were not surprised by the content and 54.9% considering the leak as evidence of a legitimate investigation. Flávio's candidacy was seen as weakened by 64.1% of respondents (45.1% very weakened + 19% weakened).

item.title: 'Quarteto fantástico' do Flamengo está de volta? Relembre quem eram os rubro-negros campeões de 1958 pelo Brasil
item.description: Flamengo has four players called up for the World Cup for the first time in 68 years, matching its 1958 feat. Danilo, Alex Sandro, Léo Pereira and Lucas Paquetá are in Brazil's final squad for the 2026 World Cup, just like Zagallo, Dida, Joel and Moacir were in 1958. The club may also have up to five additional players representing other South American nations.

item.title: O que pensam aliados de Flávio e Caiado sobre Joaquim Barbosa na disputa ao Planalto
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado believe Joaquim Barbosa has lost the timing to be competitive in the 2026 presidential race, having been absent from public life for years. They argue he no longer embodies either the 'justiceiro' image — now associated with Alexandre de Moraes — or the 'anti-PT magistrate' figure, which has been taken over by Sergio Moro among Bolsonaro voters.

item.title: Flávio “irmão do Vorcaro” Bolsonaro e as próximas pesquisas
item.description: The author criticizes the tendency of Brazilian voters to repeat past mistakes by supporting inefficient politicians, using Flávio Bolsonaro — nicknamed 'brother of Vorcaro' — as an example. Despite a lack of significant achievements, voters remain loyal to figures tied to Bolsonarism. The post was originally published on O Antagonista.

item.title: Flávio cai 6 pontos no 2º turno após mensagens a Vorcaro, indica AtlasIntel
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) dropped six percentage points in voter intention for a potential runoff against Lula (PT), according to an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg survey released Tuesday, the 19th. The decline followed the leak of messages sent by the senator to banker Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Master. Lula now leads with 48.9%, compared to 41.8% for the PL candidate.

item.title: Fora da Copa, Bento desabafa nas redes após perder vaga para Weverton: 'As coisas não acabam por aqui'
item.description: Goalkeeper Bento expressed disappointment on social media after being left out of Brazil's final squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, thanking supporters and stating 'things don't end here'. Goalkeeping coach Taffarel clarified that Weverton was selected over Bento due to experience, not a recent error, citing Alisson and Ederson's injuries and emphasizing Weverton's extensive international background with over 50 caps and 10 appearances for Brazil.

item.title: AtlasIntel: áudio com Vorcaro impacta eleitor e Flávio perde fôlego na disputa com Lula
item.description: The leak of an audio in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro demands money from banker Daniel Vorcaro was known by 95.6% of voters and negatively impacted his campaign, reducing his support by over five points. According to the AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll, Lula leads with 47.0% against Flávio’s 34.3% in the first round, a nearly 13-point advantage. In a potential runoff, Lula maintains over a seven-point lead, while Renan Santos (Missão) gained third place with 6.9% without offsetting Flávio’s losses.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cai 5 pontos em pesquisa após divulgação de troca de mensagens com Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro dropped over five points in the AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll, falling from 39.7% to 34.3% after messages with Daniel Vorcaro were disclosed, while Lula rose to 47%. Renan Santos and Romeu Zema gained from the bolsonarist decline, and the scenario without Flávio shows no candidate can inherit his base, strengthening Lula’s position in a potential runoff.

item.title: Atlas: 51,7% veem evidências de envolvimento de Flávio Bolsonaro com escândalo do Master após áudio
item.description: Atlas/Bloomberg poll shows 51.7% of Brazilian voters who became aware of the audio exchanges between Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro believe there is evidence of the senator’s involvement in the Banco Master scandal. Meanwhile, 33.3% argue the conversations were legitimate efforts to secure funding for the film 'Dark Horse', a tribute to Jair Bolsonaro. The fallout is severe: 47.1% of respondents say they would no longer vote for Flávio Bolsonaro for president following the revelations.

item.title: Conselho de Ética vota nova suspensão de Pollon; governistas veem chance de aprovar
item.description: The House Ethics Committee is set to vote on Tuesday, the 19th, on a report by Deputy Ricardo Maia (MDB-BA) recommending the procedural validity of disciplinary proceedings against Marcos Pollon (PL-MS) for defamatory statements against the House presidency made in August 2025. Government allies see the vote as an opportunity to approve Pollon’s suspension, following prior disciplinary actions against him in the same committee.

item.title: João Pedro é eleito melhor jogador do Chelsea na temporada horas depois de ficar fora de convocação para Copa do Mundo
item.description: João Pedro was named Chelsea's Player of the Season, receiving over 60% of fan votes, just hours after being left out of Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad. The forward had an outstanding debut season with 20 goals and five assists in 49 appearances, including key performances in the Club World Cup and a hat-trick against Aston Villa.

item.title: Rodinei reage após convocação de Ancelotti e manda recado nas redes: ‘Ainda sou brasileiro’
item.description: Right-back Rodinei, currently playing for Olympiacos, responded to his omission from Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad by Carlo Ancelotti with a social media post stating that, although not selected, he will continue giving his best in Greece and reminded everyone: 'I am still Brazilian'.

item.title: Galípolo vai ao Senado para prestar esclarecimentos sobre transações envolvendo o Master e o BRB
item.description: Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo appears before the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee to explain financial operations involving Banco Master, amid pressure to install a parliamentary inquiry (CPI) into the bank. The hearing follows leaked audio in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested R$134 million from the bank's owner to finance a biopic of former President Jair Bolsonaro. Galípolo is expected to criticize Roberto Campos Neto's management during the Bolsonaro administration.

item.title: Danilo pode não atuar mais pelo Botafogo após convocação para a Copa pela seleção
item.description: Danilo, called up for the World Cup, asked not to play for Botafogo against Corinthians to avoid injury and prevent a transfer block to another Brazilian club in 2026. His availability for upcoming matches in the Sudamericana and Brasileirão is uncertain, with club management dissatisfied and his representatives unhappy over delayed payments. Although his sale after the tournament is nearly certain, coach Franclim Carvalho may already be planning a team without him, especially after Huguinho impressed as a replacement.

item.title: As eleições brasileiras e as perspectivas para o BRICS+
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections are affecting Brazil's engagement in BRICS+, with the Lula government maintaining only a formally active posture amid domestic political uncertainty and congressional opposition. Ex-president Jair Bolsonaro's explicit statements that he would withdraw Brazil from the bloc if returned to power heighten strategic uncertainty about the continuity of Brazilian participation. Although Brazil continues to perform symbolic roles — such as advocating for expansion and hosting preparatory meetings — progress toward deeper integration, including local currency payments and joint industrial policies, has significantly slowed.

item.title: Os dois objetivos e os dois abacaxis que Flávio Bolsonaro tem pela frente nesta semana
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces two strategic objectives and at least two significant challenges (pineapples to peel) this week, according to an exclusive subscriber-only article. The content does not disclose specific details, indicating that full access requires registration and login on the publication’s website.

item.title: Datafolha: 59% dos brasileiros dizem não ter sabido da rejeição de indicado de Lula ao STF pelo Senado
item.description: A Datafolha poll reveals that 59% of Brazilians were unaware of the Senate's rejection of Lula's Supreme Court nominee, equivalent to 6 in 10 respondents. Among the 41% who were informed, 53% believe the government emerged weaker from the defeat, while only 7% see it as stronger. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between March 12 and 13, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Oposição planeja estratégia eleitoral em 4 Estados do Nordeste e PT pode perder hegemonia
item.description: The opposition plans to exploit public security as the PT's main weakness in four Northeastern states (Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, Piauí, and Bahia), where homicide rates exceed the national average. Bahia and Ceará rank among the worst in the country, with Fortaleza and Salvador among the most violent capitals. Former mayor ACM Neto (União Brasil) leads the criticism against PT governor Jerônimo Rodrigues in Bahia, with a poll showing a technical tie (41% to 37%).

item.title: Cotada para vice diz a Flávio Bolsonaro não ser ‘extremista’: ‘Converso do PT ao PL’
item.description: Deputy Simone Marquetto (PP-SP), tipped as a vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) ticket, said she is not an extremist lawmaker and maintains dialogue with politicians from the PT to the PL, emphasizing her conciliatory, center-right profile. She highlighted her social work, ties to the Catholic Church, and stated she will not run for re-election, claiming an executive profile. The meeting took place during a tense moment for Flávio Bolsonaro, following leaked conversations in which he asked banker Daniel Vorcaro for money for the film Dark Horse.

item.title: Torcida do Brasil 'enlouqueceu' com 'conto de fadas' de Neymar, diz jornal
item.description: Neymar's call-up for the 2026 World Cup sparked widespread joy among Brazilian fans, with international media describing it as a 'fairy tale'. The Santos striker, aged 34 and returning after over two years away from the national team, was celebrated as an emotional comeback despite his injury-plagued recent career. The notable omission of Chelsea's João Pedro was highlighted, while Vinícius Júnior and Raphinha were also emphasized in the selections.

item.title: Aliados de Lula se dividem sobre estratégia de insistir na indicação de Messias para o STF
item.description: Allies of President Lula are divided over whether to persist with the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The more combative faction argues the government should not yield to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s demands, while pragmatists believe the nomination should be delayed for a more opportune moment. The exclusive report reveals internal rifts within Lula’s coalition over the STF appointment strategy.

item.title: Dino diz ter sido ameaçado por funcionária de companhia aérea
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino reported being threatened with death by an airline employee who, upon seeing his name on a boarding pass, said it would be "better to kill than to insult" him. He linked the incident to rising electoral tensions and urged companies to promote civic education to prevent violence against public officials. STF President Edson Fachin condemned the threat, emphasizing that ideological differences must not justify hatred, violence, or personal attacks, and called for serenity and democratic commitment in Brazil.

item.title: Sinais de freio em ano eleitoral
item.description: In March, Brazil's economy contracted by 0.7% according to the Central Bank's Economic Activity Index, although the first quarter still showed 1.3% growth due to strong agribusiness performance early in the year. However, outlook for the rest of 2026 is concerning, with rising production costs and falling international prices for agricultural commodities. The market raised its year-end Selic rate projection in the Focus survey, signaling expectations for a more prolonged monetary tightening cycle.

item.title: Disputa inglória
item.description: The success of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy now depends on external factors, particularly revelations from Federal Police investigations and the plea bargain of former banker Daniel Vorcaro. His credibility has been damaged by concealing his relationship with Vorcaro, raising suspicions about what else he might be hiding. The article suggests that new scandals could emerge and jeopardize his electoral viability.

item.title: ‘Dark Horse’: petistas acionam TSE para impedir estreia de filme sobre Jair Bolsonaro até eleições
item.description: The Prerrogativas group and federal deputy Rogério Correia (PT-MG), allies of President Lula, have filed a request with the TSE to investigate the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', a biopic about Jair Bolsonaro's political career that received R$61 million from businessman Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master. The action seeks to block the film’s September premiere — just one month before the 2026 presidential elections — on grounds that it may constitute illegal campaign financing aimed at influencing the vote.
